facts: JanusDDG is a deep learning model developed by researchers at the University of Turin's Computational Biomedicine Unit.
The model predicts protein stability changes (ΔΔG) from amino acid sequences.
JanusDDG employs a two-fronts multi-head attention mechanism.
The model integrates thermodynamic constraints to improve the accuracy of protein stability predictions.
JanusDDG is a deep learning framework that predicts protein stability changes (ΔΔG) caused by mutations.
The model uses a bidirectional cross-attention transformer architecture.
JanusDDG achieves state-of-the-art performance in predicting ΔΔG from sequence alone.
The framework has significant applications for functional protein design and understanding disease-related mutations.
Protein stability is measured by the change in Gibbs free energy (ΔΔG).
JanusDDG is a deep learning model that predicts ΔΔG using only amino acid sequences.
JanusDDG can predict stability changes for multi-mutations.
The model complies with thermodynamic principles through antisymmetry and transitivity properties.
JanusDDG is a sequence-based deep learning model for predicting protein stability changes (ΔΔG).
The model incorporates thermodynamic principles such as antisymmetry and transitivity.
JanusDDG was evaluated on benchmark datasets including S669, S461, S96, PTmut-NR, and PTmul-D.
The model shows consistent performance for double mutations regardless of spatial or sequence distance.
JanusDDG is a sequence-based deep learning model for predicting protein stability changes upon mutation.
The model combines protein language model embeddings with a bidirectional cross-attention architecture.
JanusDDG outperforms existing predictors on low-sequence-identity benchmarks like the S96 and PTmul-NR datasets.
The model effectively predicts multiple mutations, showing superior performance compared to current models.
JanusDDG is a protein stability prediction model that uses ESM2 protein embeddings.
The model employs a Bidirectional Cross-Attention Transformer architecture.
Evaluation of JanusDDG includes multiple datasets such as S669 and S461.
The model builds on established methods like FoldX and POPMUSIC.
JanusDDG has three variants: fine-tuned, antisymmetric by construction, and base.
The Pearson correlation for single mutations in JanusDDG ranges from 0.54 to 0.84.
JanusDDG achieved a Pearson correlation of 0.84 on the Ssym benchmark dataset.
JanusDDG's mean squared error on the K2369 dataset is 1.14.
